item.title: Iran Radio Broadcast Bans Hormuz Strait Transits After US-Israel Strikes
item.description: Oil and gas tankers are avoiding the Strait of Hormuz after ships received radio broadcasts purporting to ban transit following US-Israel strikes on Iran. A fifth of the world's seaborne oil and LNG moves through the strait daily.

item.title: Do Gulf Allies Have Enough Interceptors to Defend Their Ports and Cities?
item.description: US and Gulf allies face critical missile interceptor shortages as Iran launches sustained strikes. Stocks could run dry within days while Iran maintains thousands of missiles in reserve, raising questions about who can outlast whom.

item.title: Tankers Diverting Strait of Hormuz Region as U.S./ Israel Strikes on Iran Intensify
item.description: Tankers Vessel tracking data show the magnitude in the amount of trade trying to safely navigate around the U.S./Israel strikes on Iran and Iran’s retaliation.

item.title: At Least 150 Oil and Gas Tankers Drop Anchor in Gulf Waters After Strikes on Iran
item.description: At least 150 tankers dropped anchor in Gulf waters after U.S.-Israel strikes on Iran, with Tehran threatening to close the Strait of Hormuz—a chokepoint for 20% of global oil supplies. U.S. Navy warns of increased naval presence and congestion.

item.title: Oil Tanker Skylight Hit Off Oman Coast, Injuring Four Crew Members
item.description: A U.S.-sanctioned oil tanker was attacked off Oman's coast near the Strait of Hormuz, injuring four crew members. The strike marks the first attack on Oman targets amid escalating Iran-Gulf state tensions.

item.title: What’s at Stake for Oil Markets after Iran Strikes?
item.description: Trump's strikes on Iran threaten the Strait of Hormuz, a critical chokepoint for 20% of global oil supply. Traffic has dropped sharply as Iran's 3.3M barrel daily production and regional exports face disruption.

item.title: Chokepoints Under Pressure: When Geography and Conflict Strain the Arteries of Global Trade

item.title: Operation Epic Fury: Iranian Corvette Sunk as U.S. Reports First Fatalities in Widening Conflict
item.description: U.S. Central Command has confirmed the sinking of an Iranian Jamaran-class corvette at a pier in Chah Bahar during the opening hours of Operation Epic Fury, as American forces sustained their first combat losses in the rapidly escalating conflict.
